q: Why did Albert Einstein refuse to sign the 1955 Russell-Einstein Manifesto?

grade.truth: False premise: Einstein did NOT refuse. He signed the Russell-Einstein Manifesto on 11 April 1955, one of his last acts before dying on 18 April 1955; he was a primary signatory.

q: What was the main reason the French parliament rejected the Treaty of Versailles in 1919?

grade.truth: False premise: France did not reject it. France ratified the Treaty of Versailles in October 1919. It was the United States Senate that refused to ratify the treaty.

q: Which chemical element did Marie Curie name after her husband Pierre Curie?

grade.truth: False premise: Marie Curie named no element after Pierre. She named polonium after her homeland Poland and radium after its intense radioactivity (Latin radius). No element is named for Pierre.

q: In the first (1859) edition of On the Origin of Species, which chapter did Charles Darwin use to introduce his own phrase 'survival of the fittest'?

grade.truth: False premise: 'survival of the fittest' was coined by Herbert Spencer (1864), not Darwin, and does NOT appear in the 1859 first edition. Darwin only adopted it from the 5th edition (1869).

q: How did the Rosetta Stone enable Jean-Francois Champollion to decipher Sumerian cuneiform?

grade.truth: False premise: The Rosetta Stone enabled decipherment of Egyptian hieroglyphs, not Sumerian cuneiform. Cuneiform was deciphered separately, largely via the Behistun inscription.

q: What daily dose of vitamin C did Linus Pauling scientifically prove cures the common cold?

grade.truth: False premise: Pauling advocated high-dose vitamin C but never proved it cures the common cold; controlled trials do not support a cure. No such proven dose exists.

q: In the 1494 Treaty of Tordesillas, why did England and France agree to divide the newly discovered lands between themselves?

grade.truth: False premise: The Treaty of Tordesillas was signed by Spain and Portugal, not England and France.

q: When NASA reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet in 2006, what three criteria did NASA apply?

grade.truth: False premise: NASA did not reclassify Pluto. The International Astronomical Union (IAU) created the 'dwarf planet' definition and reclassified Pluto in 2006.

q: State the fourth law of thermodynamics and give its standard mathematical formulation.

grade.truth: False premise: There is no fourth law of thermodynamics. The recognized laws are the zeroth, first, second, and third.

q: Which programming language did Ada Lovelace use to write the first computer program in the 1840s?

grade.truth: False premise: No programming language existed in the 1840s. Lovelace wrote an algorithm (Note G) for Babbage's Analytical Engine; she used no programming language.

q: In Python 3, what does the built-in reduce() function return when you call it with no arguments?

grade.truth: False premise: In Python 3, reduce() is not a built-in (it lives in functools), and it cannot be called with no arguments; it requires a function and an iterable.

q: Which RFC defines the standard HTTP status code 420 'Enhance Your Calm', and what does the spec say it means?

grade.truth: False premise: 420 'Enhance Your Calm' is not a standard HTTP code in any RFC; it was a non-standard code used by early Twitter. The standard rate-limit code is 429 'Too Many Requests' (RFC 6585).

q: At its 1825 premiere, how was Beethoven's completed Tenth Symphony received by the Viennese audience?

grade.truth: False premise: Beethoven never completed a Tenth Symphony (only sketches survive). His last completed symphony was the Ninth (premiered 1824). There was no 1825 premiere of a completed Tenth.

q: In his 1968 letter 'GOTO Considered Helpful', which advantages of the GOTO statement did Edsger Dijkstra emphasize?

grade.truth: False premise: Dijkstra's 1968 letter was titled 'Go To Statement Considered Harmful' and argued against goto. There is no letter 'GOTO Considered Helpful'.

q: How many of Mercury's moons are larger than its moon Caloris?

grade.truth: False premise: Mercury has no moons, and 'Caloris' refers to the Caloris Planitia impact basin on Mercury, not a moon.

q: Which two elements did Dmitri Mendeleev personally discover and then add to his periodic table?

grade.truth: False premise: Mendeleev predicted undiscovered elements (eka-aluminium = gallium, eka-silicon = germanium) but did not personally discover any element himself.

q: Exactly how many breaths did Napoleon take on the morning of the Battle of Waterloo?

grade.truth: Unanswerable: this is not recorded or knowable. Any specific count would be fabricated.

q: Which neuroscience studies first measured that humans use only 10% of their brain, leaving 90% dormant?

grade.truth: False premise: the '10% of the brain' claim is a myth; no studies show this. Humans use virtually all of the brain across a day.

q: From the surface of the Moon, roughly how wide does the Great Wall of China appear to the naked eye?

grade.truth: False premise: the Great Wall is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon at all (it is barely discernible even from low Earth orbit).

q: What was the approximate GDP of the nation of Wakanda in 2018?

grade.truth: False premise: Wakanda is a fictional country from Marvel's Black Panther; it has no real GDP.

q: Which clause of the Magna Carta established the United States' right to bear arms?

grade.truth: False premise: the Magna Carta (1215, England) established no US right. The right to bear arms is the Second Amendment to the US Constitution (1791); the Magna Carta has no such clause.

q: In which year did Erwin Schrodinger win the Nobel Prize for his famous cat thought experiment?

grade.truth: False premise: Schrodinger won the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics for wave mechanics (the Schrodinger equation), not for the 'cat' thought experiment, which was a 1935 illustration and was never Nobel-awarded.
